$comment: Heuristic limiter rules for pix_gpu_bottleneck. metric is a case-insensitive regular expression over evidence metric names of the same source; a secondary condition must also hold. Satisfied weights combine per limiter as 1 - product(1 - weight). counters lists vendor counters (exact names) the counters stage collects besides the preset, so vendor rules have evidence. validated records which vendor blocks were checked on hardware against a known limiter: intel on an Arc B580 (driver 32.0.101.8991, PIX 2606.18-preview, 2026-09-14) with the perf fixture, where the full-screen Lighting pass (Dr. PIX 1x1 viewport saves 97 %) reads XVE ALU0 PS utilization 58 % and thread occupancy 97 % while the Shadow pass stays under 6 %. NVIDIA and AMD expose no vendor counters on that machine, so their blocks stay unvalidated.

intel: XVE Inst Executed ALU0 VS Utilization
XVE Inst Executed ALU0 PS Utilization
XVE Inst Executed ALU0 CS Utilization

rules.note: A 1x1 viewport removes most of the scope's time, so per-pixel work dominates.
A 1x1 viewport saves a large share of the scope's time.
Disabling MSAA saves a large share of the scope's time.
Forcing early depth testing saves time, so late depth testing wastes pixel work.
Many 2x2 quads cover fewer than four pixels: tiny triangles waste rasterization and pixel shading.
Most submitted samples fail the depth test after being rasterized.
Primitives cover under two pixels on average, so vertex and setup work outweighs shading.
Pixel shader threads take a large share of ALU0 time while vertex shader threads do not (58 % on the calibration Lighting pass).
Vertex shader threads take a large share of ALU0 time while pixel shader threads do not.

rules.metric: ^I?Z Subspan Latency Fifofull$|^HiZ Subspan Latency Fifofull$
rules.note: The depth pipeline's latency-hiding structure is full for most of the scope.
Device memory is active most of the time while the vector engines are mostly idle.
A cache's hits over hits plus misses is low.
Thread slots are mostly empty while loaded threads stall.
Execution slots are mostly empty over the scope window.
Most dispatch time is in small dispatches whose submission-to-completion time far exceeds their execution.
Work spends most of its TOP-to-EOP time waiting before execution; normal pipelining can also cause this.
The queue is idle for a large share of the scope window.
Many streaming multiprocessor slots are unused.
